claim: Within-group genetic diversity varied substantially between groups ranging from less than 1 SNP/10 kb within the three CH samples to ~16 SNPs/10 kb in Ldon4.
source: Within-group genetic diversity varied substantially between groups ranging from less than 1 SNP/10 kb within the three CH samples to ~16 SNPs/10 kb in Ldon4 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes a finding from the diversity analysis.

claim: Most within-group segregating variation was group-specific: no SNPs segregated within all eight groups.
source: Most within-group segregating variation was group-specific: no SNPs segregated within all eight groups.
evidence: This describes a finding from the diversity analysis.

claim: The most widespread polymorphisms are 4 SNPs shared between 6 groups and 25 SNPs segregating in at least five of the eight groups and might be putative candidates for SNPs under balancing selection.
source: The most widespread polymorphisms are 4 SNPs shared between 6 groups and 25 SNPs segregating in at least five of the eight groups and might be putative candidates for SNPs under balancing selection (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is speculation based on the diversity analysis.

claim: A total of 940 large CNVs (duplications and deletions ≥ 25 kb) were found, an average of ~6 per sample.
source: In total, 940 large CNVs were found, an average of ~6 per sample.
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: 75% of large CNVs had a length ≤ 40 kb and only ~3% were > 100 kb with the largest variant of 675 kb.
source: 75% of these large variants had a length ≤ 40 kb and only ~3% were > 100 kb with the largest variant of 675 kb (Supplementary file 6, Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: Most very large CNVs (> 100 kb) were located on chromosome 35.
source: Most of these very large variants ( > 100 kb), were located on chromosome 35 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: All very large CNVs on chromosome 35 were either deletions or duplications close to the 3' and 5' end of the chromosome, respectively, and all duplications contained the previously described CD1/LD1 locus.
source: Interestingly, those were all either deletions or duplications close to the 3' and 5' end of the chromosome, respectively. All those duplications contained the previously described CD1/LD1 locus (Figure 7—figure supplement 2; Sunkin et al., 2001; Kündig et al., 1999; Lemley et al., 1999).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis, supported by citations.

claim: At least 9 different duplicated sequences spanning the CD1/LD1 locus were found, present in 13 of the 151 isolates.
source: In total, we found at least 9 different duplicated sequences spanning the CD1/LD1 locus, present in 13 of our 151 isolates (Supplementary file 7, 8).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: The frequency of large CNVs varied among chromosomes but was not associated with chromosome length for duplications (Pearson correlation -0.06, p-value 0.74) and showed a weak negative correlation for deletions (Pearson correlation 0.32, p-value 0.05).
source: The frequency of large CNVs varied among chromosomes but was not associated with chromosome length for duplications (Pearson correlation -0.06, p-value 0.74) and showed a weak negative correlation for deletions (Pearson correlation 0.32, p-value 0.05) (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This describes a statistical result from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: A total of 183 and 62 'unique' duplications and deletions, respectively, were identified when clustering each variant type across all samples based on chromosomal location.
source: We identified a total of 183 and 62 'unique' duplications and deletions, respectively, when clustering each variant type across all samples based on chromosomal location (see Materials and methods, Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: Approximately half the CNVs were located at the chromosome ends (22% and 26% starting within 15 kb of chromosome 5' and 3' ends, respectively).
source: Approximately half the CNVs were located at the chromosome ends, that is 22% and 26% starting within 15 kb of chromosome 5' and 3' ends, respectively.
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: The majority of large CNVs were present in only a single sample, but some were much more widespread – the most frequent being present in 42 different samples and one variant being present in eight different groups.
source: The majority of large CNVs, were present in only a single sample, but some were much more widespread – the most frequent being present in 42 different samples and one variant being present in eight different groups (Figure 7—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: 28% (69 of 245) of all large CNVs were present in both species L. donovani and L. infantum.
source: 28% (69 of 245) of all variants were present in both species (Figure 7—figure supplement 4B; Supplementary file 7) and we investigated those in more detail.
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: A 25 kb long deletion on chromosome 27 was present in 15% of all samples and across four of the different identified groups including both species.
source: The 25 kb long deletion on chromosome 27 was present in 15% of all samples and across four of the different identified groups including both species (Figure 7A, deletion 150 in Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: The deletion on chromosome 27 always occurred on a disomic background resulting in the loss of the allele.
source: It always occurred on a disomic background resulting in the loss of the allele.
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: The 17 genes present in the deleted region on chromosome 27 were enriched for the GO term 'cilium-dependent motility' due to a single gene annotated as a 'radial spoke protein 3'.
source: The 17 genes present in the deleted region were enriched for the GO term 'cilium-dependent motility' due to a single gene annotated as a 'radial spoke protein 3' (LINF_270011200 v41, LinJ.27.2550 v38) (Figure 7C).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: A putative amastin gene (LINF_270011400 v41, LinJ.27.2550 v38) – part of a large gene family that has an essential role during infection of the mammalian host – was present in the deleted region on chromosome 27.
source: However, other genes including a putative amastin (LINF_270011400 v41, LinJ.27.2550 v38) – part of a large gene family that has an essential role during infection of the mammalian host (de Paiva et al., 2015) – were also present in this region.
evidence: This is an observation supported by a citation about the function of amastins.

claim: A duplication found on chromosome 35 was only present in a single sample in each, the Ldon1 and Linf1, group and overlapped with the CD1/LD1 locus.
source: The duplication found on chromosome 35 was only present in a single sample in each, the Ldon1 and Linf1, group and overlapped with the CD1/LD1 locus (Figure 7B; duplication 215 in Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: In Ldon1, the duplication on chromosome 35 showed a 2-copy increase on a disomic background, suggesting it was either homozygous for a duplication haplotype or heterozygous with one normal and one 2-copy duplication haplotype.
source: In Ldon1, it showed a 2-copy increase on a disomic background, suggesting it was either homozygous for a duplication haplotype or heterozygous with one normal and one 2-copy duplication haplotype.
evidence: This is an inference based on the copy number analysis.

claim: In Linf1, the sample with the duplication on chromosome 35 has a single copy duplication on a trisomic background.
source: In contrast, the sample from Linf1 has a single copy duplication on a trisomic background.
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: 66 genes are present in the insertion on chromosome 35 enriched for several GO categories.
source: 66 genes are present in the insertion enriched for several GO categories (Figure 7C).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Copy number variation affected 91.5% of genes (7,625 / 8,330), but most CNVs are rare.
source: CN variation affected 91.5% of genes (7,625 / 8,330; Figure 8A, Supplementary file 9), but most CNVs are rare (Figure 8A).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Only 3.6% of all genes (304) showed a median copy number change ( ≤ -1 or ≥ 1) across samples with 103 genes decreased and 201 increased, respectively.
source: Only 3.6% of all genes (304) showed a median copy number change ( ≤ -1 or ≥ 1) across samples with 103 genes decreased and 201 increased, respectively (Figure 8B).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: The 103 genes with frequently reduced copy number showed GO term enrichments for the biological processes 'cation transport', 'transmembrane transport', 'fatty acid biosynthesis' and 'localization'.
source: Enrichment tests for the 103 genes with frequently reduced copy number showed GO term enrichments for the biological processes "cation transport", "transmembrane transport", "fatty acid biosynthesis" and "localization" (median CN change across samples ≤ 1, Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The 201 genes that were regularly increased showed enrichment for several terms including 'modulation by symbiont of host protein kinase-mediated signal transduction', 'cell adhesion' and 'drug catabolic process'.
source: The 201 genes that were regularly increased showed enrichment for several terms including but not exclusive to "modulation by symbiont of host protein kinase-mediated signal transduction", "cell adhesion" and "drug catabolic process" (median CN change across samples ≥ 1, for full list see Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Only a subset of 52 genes (0.6%) showed frequently high gene copy number increases (median ≥ 4 across all samples).
source: Only a subset of 52 genes (0.6%) showed frequently high gene copy number increases (median ≥ 4 across all samples).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Enriched GO terms for genes with frequently high copy number increases largely overlapped with enrichments of genes including small CN increases with the additional enrichment of 'response to active oxygen species'.
source: Enriched GO terms largely overlapped with enrichments of genes including small CN increases with the additional enrichment of "response to active oxygen species" (Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: GO categories enriched in genes with frequent copy number changes might indicate functions on which there is frequent or strong selection pressure.
source: Those categories might indicate functions on which there is frequent or strong selection pressure.
evidence: This is speculation based on the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Median gene copy number was positively correlated among groups (Pearson correlation for pairwise comparisons between 0.8 and 0.91).
source: Median gene copy number was positively correlated among groups (Figure 8C, Pearson correlation for pairwise comparisons between 0.8 and 0.91).
evidence: This describes a statistical result from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Despite extensive variation and shared copy number variation across groups, gene copy number still retained some phylogenetic signal.
source: Despite this extensive variation and shared copy number variation across groups, gene copy number still retained some phylogenetic signal (Figure 8D).
evidence: This describes a finding from the phylogenetic analysis of gene copy number.

claim: The H-locus amplification is involved in resistance to several unrelated drugs including antimonials.
source: The best-known genetic variant associated with drug resistance in Leishmania is the so-called H-locus: amplification of this locus is involved in resistance to several unrelated drugs including antimonials (Callahan and Beverley, 1991; Dias et al., 2007; Grondin et al., 1993; Leprohon et al., 2009; Marchini et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The four genes at the H-locus had an increased gene copy number in 30% of the samples (CN +1 to +44) and a reduced copy number in 9% (CN −1).
source: In our dataset, the four genes at this locus had an increased gene copy number in 30% of the samples (CN +1 to +44) and a reduced copy number in 9% (CN −1; Table 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: 36% of all isolates had a copy number increase of varying degree with identical insertion boundaries that included the genes YIP1, MRPA and argininosuccinate synthase.
source: 36% of all isolates had a copy number increase of varying degree with identical insertion boundaries that included the genes YIP1, MRPA and argininosuccinate synthase (Figure 9A, Figure 9—figure supplement 1A, Table 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: The H-locus duplication was only present in groups Ldon1 and Ldon3 with median increases of approximately +4 and +2, respectively.
source: This duplication was only present in groups Ldon1 and Ldon3 with median increases of approximately +4 and +2, respectively.
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Parasites on the Indian subcontinent (largely Ldon1) have experienced the highest drug pressure of antimonials in the past and are suggested to be preadapted to this drug, and therefore have the highest prevalence and extent of CN increase at the H-locus, followed by isolates from Sudan and Ethiopia (largely Ldon3).
source: This matches the rationale that parasites on the Indian subcontinent (largely Ldon1) have experienced the highest drug pressure of antimonials in the past and are suggested to be preadapted to this drug (Dumetz et al., 2018) and therefore have the highest prevalence and extent of CN increase, followed by isolates from Sudan and Ethiopia (largely Ldon3).
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene copy number variation analysis and a citation to a previous study.

claim: The Pteridine reductase 1 gene at the H-locus may not be relevant for drug resistance as it does not show an increased gene CN along with the other genes at that locus.
source: Under this scenario, the Pteridine reductase 1 gene at the H-locus may not be relevant for the drug resistance as it does not show an increased gene CN along with the other genes at that locus (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is speculation based on the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: One isolate (LRC-L51p, Ldon5, India, 1954) had a much larger duplication in the H-locus region including the entire H-locus and spanning >45 kb with an enormous increase of ~+44 suggesting an independent insertion or amplification mechanism.
source: One other isolate, LRC-L51p (Ldon5, India, 1954), had a much larger duplication in this region including the entire H-locus and spanning >45 kb with an enormous increase of ~+44 suggesting an independent insertion or amplification mechanism (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is an observation with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Four additional isolates showed a copy number increase for only two of the genes at the H-locus, with different boundaries but always including the MRPA gene.
source: Four additional isolates showed a copy number increase for only two of the genes at the locus, with different boundaries but always including the MRPA gene (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: 45% of all isolates had an amplified copy number at the MAPK1 locus, including all isolates of Ldon1 and Ldon3 with the highest copy number increase in Ldon1 isolates of between 12 and 41 copies.
source: 45% of all isolates had an amplified copy number at this locus, including all isolates of Ldon1 and Ldon3 with the highest copy number increase in Ldon1 isolates of between 12 and 41 copies (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A, Table 2, Supplementary file 6).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Only a single L. infantum isolate had a reduced copy number of one at the MAPK1 locus.
source: Only a single L. infantum isolate had a reduced copy number of one.
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Increased copy number of MAPK1 is associated with isolates from geographical locations with high historical antimonial drug pressures such as the Indian subcontinent and to a lesser extend Africa.
source: Increased copy number of MAPK1 is thus associated with isolates from geographical locations with high historical antimonial drug pressures such as the Indian subcontinent and to a lesser extend Africa.
evidence: This is an inference based on the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Copy number at the AQP1 locus was reduced in 6% and increased in 35% of all isolates with small effect sizes (CN −2 to −1 and +1 to +3) but at least one copy of the locus was always present.
source: In our dataset, copy number at this locus was reduced in 6% and increased in 35% of all isolates with small effect sizes (CN −2 to −1 and +1 to +3) but at least one copy of the locus was always present (Figure 9—figure supplement 2B, Table 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: Neither LdMT, Ros3 or a hypothetical protein deleted together with LdMT in a drug selection experiment showed a reduction in gene copy number across the 151 isolates.
source: Neither LdMT, Ros3 or a hypothetical protein deleted together with LdMT in a drug selection experiment (Shaw et al., 2016), showed a reduction in gene copy number across our 151 isolates (Figure 9—figure supplement 2C, Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene copy number variation analysis.

claim: No SNP variation was present in two codons (A691, E197) putatively associated with Miltefosine resistance.
source: Moreover, no SNP variation was present in two codons (A691, E197; Shaw et al., 2016) putatively associated with drug resistance (Table 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from the SNP analysis.

claim: The Miltefosine sensitivity locus (MSL) was recently identified as a deletion associated with treatment failure in a clinical study of patients with VL in Brazil.
source: The Miltefosine sensitivity locus (MSL) was recently identified as a deletion associated with treatment failure in a clinical study of patients with VL in Brazil (Carnielli et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a research study.

claim: Genotyping of the MSL showed clinal variation in the presence of the locus ranging from 95% in North East Brazil to <5% in the South East (N = 157), while no deletion was found in the Old World.
source: In the same study, further genotyping of the MSL showed clinal variation in the presence of the locus ranging from 95% in North East Brazil to <5% in the South East (N = 157), while no deletion was found in the Old World.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a research study.

claim: The entire MSL locus including all four genes was completely deleted in four samples of the Linf1 group including two of the four samples from Brazil (Cha001 1974, WC 2007) and in the two samples from Honduras (HN167 1998, HN336 1993) with deletion boundaries coinciding with those reported previously.
source: The entire locus including all four genes (Table 2) was completely deleted in four of our samples of the Linf1 group including two of the four samples from Brazil (Cha001 1974, WC 2007) and in the two samples from Honduras (HN167 1998, HN336 1993) (Figure 9B, Supplementary file 9) with deletion boundaries coinciding with those reported previously (Carnielli et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: Another isolate (IMT373cl1, collected in Portugal, 2005) showed a deletion of a larger region (90 kb) at the MSL, reducing the local chromosome copy number from four to two.
source: Another isolate, IMT373cl1 (collected in Portugal, 2005) showed a deletion of a larger region (90 kb), reducing the local chromosome copy number from four to two (Figure 9B).
evidence: This describes a finding from the copy number variation analysis.

claim: In both L. donovani and L. infantum, the α statistic was negative, with −0.19 and −0.34, respectively, showing an excess of non-synonymous polymorphisms.
source: In both, L. donovani and L. infantum, α was negative, with −0.19 and −0.34, respectively, showing an excess of non-synonymous polymorphisms but lacking a clear biological interpretation.
evidence: This describes a finding from the selection analysis.

claim: Out of 8234 genes tested for departure of neutrality using the McDonald-Kreitman test, only two and four genes showed signs of positive selection (p-value<0.05, FDR = 1) and 11 and 12 an excess of non-synonymous differences (p-value<0.05, FDR = 1) for L. donovani and L. infantum, respectively.
source: Out of 8234 genes tested for departure of neutrality using the McDonald-Kreitman test, only two and four genes showed signs of positive selection (p-value<0.05, FDR = 1) and 11 and 12 an excess of non-synonymous differences (p-value<0.05, FDR = 1) for L. donovani and L. infantum, respectively (Figure 9—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This describes a finding from the selection analysis.

claim: One of the genes with putative signs of adaptive evolution in L. donovani (LINF_330040400 v41, LinJ.33.3220 v38) was previously associated with in vivo enhanced virulence and increased parasite burden in vitro for L. major when overexpressed.
source: Interestingly, one of the genes with putative signs of adaptive evolution in L. donovani (LINF_330040400 v41, LinJ.33.3220 v38) was previously associated with in vivo enhanced virulence and increased parasite burden in vitro for L. major when overexpressed (Reiling et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an observation supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The gene LINF_330040400 contained nine missense, 3 synonymous and 19 upstream/intergenic SNP-variants differentially fixed between L. donovani and L. infantum, which might provide further candidates for differences in virulence between both species.
source: In our dataset, this gene contained nine missense, 3 synonymous and 19 upstream/intergenic SNP-variants differentially fixed between L. donovani and L. infantum (Supplementary file 4), which might provide further candidates for differences in virulence between both species.
evidence: This is speculation based on the SNP analysis.

claim: The terms 'protein phosphorylation', 'microtubule-based movement' and 'movement of cell or subcellular component' were enriched in five, three and two out of the nine tested SNP sets, respectively, for group-specific SNPs with high or moderate effect.
source: While most enrichment terms were specific to one marker set, the terms 'protein phosphorylation', 'microtubule-based movement' and 'movement of cell or subcellular component' were enriched in five, three and two out of the nine tested SNP sets, respectively (Figure 9—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: More group specific GO enrichments with potentially more easily interpretable biological implications include 'response to immune response of other organism involved in symbiotic interaction' for Ldon1, 'mismatch repair' for Linf1 in response to oxidative stress and 'pathogenesis' for the L. infantum – L. donovani species comparison.
source: More group specific enrichments with potentially more easily interpretable biological implications include 1) 'response to immune response of other organism involved in symbiotic interaction' for Ldon1, 2) 'mismatch repair' for Linf1 in response to oxidative stress and 3) 'pathogenesis' for the L. infantum – L. donovani species comparison (Figure 9—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This describes a finding from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: For the species comparison, the enrichment of the term 'pathogenesis' was due to fixed differences of putative functional relevance in genes including a protein containing a Tir chaperone (CesT) domain, a subtilisin protease and a Bardet-biedl syndrome one protein that are putative candidates for increased pathogenicity in L. donovani.
source: For the species comparison, the enrichment of the term 'pathogenesis' was due to fixed differences of putative functional relevance in genes including a protein containing a Tir chaperone (CesT) domain, a subtilisin protease and a Bardet-biedl syndrome one protein that are putative candidates for increased pathogenicity in L. donovani (Table 3, Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is speculation based on the gene ontology enrichment and SNP analysis.

claim: Tir (translocated intimin receptor) chaperones are a family of key indicators of pathogenic potential in gram-negative bacteria, where they support the type III secretion system.
source: Tir (translocated intimin receptor) chaperones are a family of key indicators of pathogenic potential in gram-negative bacteria, where they support the type III secretion system (Delahay et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Proteins containing Tir chaperone domains are almost exclusive to kinetoplastids among eukaryotes.
source: Proteins containing these domains are almost exclusive to kinetoplastids among eukaryotes.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge.

claim: In L. donovani, a subtilisin protease (SUB; Clan SB, family S8) has been found to alter regulation of the trypanothione reductase system, which is required for reactive oxygen detoxification in amastigotes and to be necessary for full virulence.
source: In L. donovani, a subtilisin protease (SUB; Clan SB, family S8), has been found to alter regulation of the trypanothione reductase system, which is required for reactive oxygen detoxification in amastigotes and to be necessary for full virulence (Swenerton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a research study.

claim: The Bardet-biedl syndrome 1 (BBS1) gene in Leishmania was shown to be involved in pathogen infectivity, with BBS1 knock-out strains showing reduced infectivity for in vitro macrophages and severely compromised ability to infect BALB/c mice.
source: The Bardet-biedl syndrome 1 (BBS1) gene in Leishmania was shown to be involved in pathogen infectivity. BBS1 knock-out strains, as promastigotes in vitro, had no apparent defects affecting growth, flagellum assembly, motility or differentiation but showed a reduced infectivity for in vitro macrophages and the ability to infect BALB/c mouse of null parasites was severely compromised (Price et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a research study.
